A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same decision-rule constraint-enforcement framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching results relocated to the appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original portfolio and DC-OPF experiments measuring optimality, constraint violations, and runtime in Table 2, plus a pre-training ablation in Table 3.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds quadratic DC-OPF evaluations and additional baseline results in Tables 2 and 6.

M1.justification: The equality projection, task/safe-network convex combination, maximum slack-ratio correction, and LP/SDP safe-network computations remain unchanged. Input-dependent alpha and separate offline safe-network computation are explained more explicitly. The straight-through estimator is proposed only as future work.

E1.justification: v2 adds quadratic-objective DC-OPF tasks on the same five power systems, retaining the linear-objective tasks and portfolio optimization. This extends task requirements within an existing domain; the input uncertainty ranges remain unchanged. Classification and reinforcement learning are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens the evaluated comparisons: EAPM is added for portfolio optimization and quadratic DC-OPF, while OSQP and post-projection using Gurobi or OSQP appear in the quadratic DC-OPF comparisons. The original comparator sets remain in the retained linear DC-OPF and portfolio results.

E3.justification: The added quadratic DC-OPF evaluation specifies solver comparisons warm-started from neural-network predictions. Existing uncertainty ranges, 100 uniformly sampled test inputs, network architecture, training budgets, and stopping tolerances are retained as documented. Warm-starting is newly specified; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun under changed initialization.

E4.justification: Table 3's pre-training ablation is identical, and the original safe-network-only LDR comparisons remain available. No new sensitivity, robustness, or error-analysis study is reported; the additional appendix results extend benchmark evaluation.

E5.justification: Both versions report test-set means and worst cases, together with average runtimes and iteration counts. Neither reports independent training repeats, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for five quadratic DC-OPF systems and EAPM on portfolio optimization. For example, Table 2 reports proposed-method mean gaps of 1.10% and 1.07% at 2.5 and 2.6 ms for quadratic 118- and 200-bus tasks. Original portfolio scores are unchanged, and all original linear DC-OPF entries are preserved in Table 5. The quadratic results are additional settings, not same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds an explicit chain-rule calculation for gradients through the maximum-based blending coefficient. The universal approximation theorem, assumptions, complexity bounds, and appendix proofs retain their substance. The expanded discussion of SDP conservatism and single-constraint exactness restates properties already present in Proposition 1.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same claims: model-agnostic enforcement of input-dependent linear constraints, non-iterative inference, universal approximation, and competitive accuracy and latency. Additional evaluations support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds focused explanations of slack maximization, gradient flow, and SDP conservatism. It discusses classification and DDPG applicability, difficulties with PPO action distributions, and potentially unstable maximum-based gradients. These extend the existing limitations discussion without changing its central feasibility–accuracy–efficiency interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a DecisionRuleNet repository reference, explicitly documents separate offline safe-network computation, and describes neural-network warm starts for solvers. Existing hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged. The earlier GAMS library link for the portfolio task is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Rubinstein's portfolio-selection retrospective, OSQP, and extrapolated alternating projections. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to gauge mappings, projections, and robust-optimization decision rules remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the blending explanation, clarifies offline-computation terminology, expands limitations and experimental discussion, and adds Appendix C.3 and funding acknowledgments. The overall section sequence remains stable. An unresolved 'Table ??' reference is introduced in Appendix C.2.

P2.justification: The central results presentation is substantially reorganized. v1 Table 2's linear DC-OPF blocks become appendix Table 5; v2 Table 2 presents portfolio and large quadratic cases with expanded comparator rows, and new Table 6 presents smaller quadratic cases. Figure 1 and Tables 1, 3, and 4 retain their substantive displays.

improvement.justification: The quadratic tasks and stronger EAPM, OSQP, and post-projection comparisons improve the evidence for practical accuracy–latency tradeoffs, while clearer computation details and limitations improve interpretability. However, new prose incorrectly claims superior optimality over post-projection: Table 2 reports 0.11% for Gurobi post-projection versus 1.10% for the proposed method on quadratic 118-bus DC-OPF. Appendix C.1 also retains only a linear-objective gap formula despite the quadratic evaluations. These inconsistencies limit the overall gain.
